internship.title: Full Stack Development Internship
internship.description: A full-stack internship that follows a feature from requirement to database, backend API, frontend UI, testing, review and deployment.
internship.learningModel: learn -> inspect -> implement -> test -> review -> iterate -> deliver
internshipExpectations: Students work from realistic requirements rather than isolated theory.
Every module has a dedicated practical and task.
Students verify work and handle failure/edge cases.
Git and code-review habits are part of the workflow.
Final work is documented and explainable.
completionRequirements: Complete all required modules and lessons.
Demonstrate the ability to explain submitted work.

modules.title: Full-Stack Onboarding
modules.description: Understand feature ownership across frontend, backend, database and deployment.

lessons.title: Full-Stack Onboarding — Internship Lesson
lessons.description: Understand feature ownership across frontend, backend, database and deployment.
learningObjectives: Apply it to the internship project.

notes.text: Understand feature ownership across frontend, backend, database and deployment.

This is an internship-style module. The goal is not only to read theory but to understand how full-stack onboarding appears in a real software team. Students inspect existing work, make a focused change, verify it, document it and respond to review feedback.

notes.alt: Full Stack Development Internship — Full-Stack Onboarding
notes.caption: Add a dedicated teaching diagram or annotated screenshot for Full-Stack Onboarding. The visual should explain the workflow, not merely decorate the lesson.

notes.text: Start with the real problem, identify the inputs and expected outcome, learn the relevant concept, then apply it to the internship project. Every important decision should be explainable in simple language.

items: Read the requirement or issue.
Inspect the existing code/design/data before changing anything.
Break the requirement into small implementation steps.
Implement the smallest correct change.
Run the relevant checks or tests.
Review the result against acceptance criteria.
Document important decisions and limitations.
Prepare the work for review.
Understand why the technique is used, not only how to type it.
Prefer maintainable solutions over clever shortcuts.
Handle success, failure and edge cases.
Keep changes focused and reviewable.
Never place secrets or credentials in source code.
Changing code before understanding the existing flow.
Ignoring error and empty states.
Skipping tests after a bug fix.
Duplicating logic instead of creating reusable boundaries.
Treating a working demo as automatically production-ready.
Use meaningful names and small functions/components.
Keep responsibilities separated.
Use Git commits that explain the change.
Test the behavior that matters to users.
Document assumptions and known limitations.
I can explain the concept without copying the notes.
I can trace the relevant code/data flow.
I can implement the basic workflow.
I can test at least one failure or edge case.
I can explain my implementation during code review.

practicals.objective: Apply Full-Stack Onboarding to a realistic internship assignment.
practicals.expectedOutput: A working, verified implementation demonstrating Full-Stack Onboarding.

requirements: Apply Full-Stack Onboarding in the internship project.
